lesson_title: Two Pulses Walk Into Each Other: Superposition
hook_text: A crest and a trough meet, the spring goes dead flat — so where did the energy go?
clip_script: Launch a pulse from each end of a spring at the same moment — a crest one way, an equal trough the other. They meet in the middle and the spring goes completely flat. Looks like they wiped each other out. But physics does not allow energy to vanish. Point a speed camera at that flat spring: the coils are still moving — up on one side, down on the other. All the energy is hiding in motion, like a skipping rope at the instant it passes through straight: no shape, maximum speed. A heartbeat later the crest climbs out one side and the trough climbs out the other, both full size, both still travelling. That is superposition: where pulses overlap, the spring adds displacements with their signs. Plus 0,4 and plus 0,2 stack into 0,6 — constructive. Plus 0,3 and minus 0,3 make zero — destructive, for exactly one instant. And after every meeting, every pulse walks away unchanged. So when a question shows you the flat spring and asks where the pulses went — nowhere. They are passing straight through.
visual_style: A neon spring stretched across the frame; a glowing crest and glowing trough race inward, collapse into a flat line that shimmers with hidden motion arrows, then burst back out; signed numbers stack and sum above the meeting point.
mood: A disappearing act exposed frame by frame.
pacing: Quick build to the collision, a long held beat on the flat spring, snap reveal of both survivors, rapid-fire rule recap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and own every interference diagram you ever meet.
